lines.narration: Why is the sky blue? The famous answer: oceans.
Blue sea below. Blue sky above. Seems obvious. It's wrong.
The Sahara sits a thousand kilometers from any sea.
So what actually paints it? Sunlight, hitting air.
Air flings blue sideways, six times harder than red.
Every patch of sky becomes a tiny blue lamp.
Aim your eyes away from the sun — deepest blue.
That's the sky. Not a mirror — a lamp.
And the ocean? Water eats red, keeps blue.
Sky and sea never painted each other. They just matched.
